name: Well-Graded Incidence Duals Characterize Paths
statement: For a finite irredundant well-graded family $H\subseteq2^X$, its incidence dual $H^\star=\{\{A\in H:x\in A\}:x\in X\}$ is well graded exactly when $H$ is a full inclusion chain. Consequently, a finite partial cube admits an irredundant well-graded representation with well-graded incidence dual exactly when it is a path.
proof: The first assertion is the essential-coordinate incidence-dual theorem for well-graded families. A full chain has a path as its one-inclusion graph, while every path admits such a chain representation when based at an endpoint.
comments: The claim concerns existence of a suitable irredundant representation. Independent coordinate complementation preserves the partial cube but can destroy dual well-gradedness.
